population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. About 64M of ~267M US adults are currently on an incretin (23.9%), and ~85M have ever used one (32%). Age check: 0.20×13 + 0.33×23.5 + 0.24×36.5 + 0.23×21 = 2.6+7.76+8.76+4.83 ≈ 23.95. Income thirds 29/24/18.5 average ≈ 23.8. Cycling: ever 32 − current 23.9 = 8.1 pp of adults (~21.6M) used and are off now. With ~40% one-year restart and five years of churn, ~38% of current users are restarters (0.38×23.9 ≈ 9.1 pp), and ~20% of those off now had already cycled once (0.2×8.1 ≈ 1.6 pp); (9.1+1.6)/32 ≈ 33%. Of the ~21.6M off now, about 7M stopped because of coverage or price (including ~1.5M pushed off during the 2029 Lilly allocation), ~8M because of side effects or 'felt flat', and the rest by choice or after reaching goal. Planned 'drug holidays' (skipped doses with no intent to stop) are not counted as stopping. Payer mix of the 64M current users: diabetes-, cardiac-, OSA- or MASH-coded coverage ~24M (up, because the ADA's dementia-risk endorsement pulled more older T2D patients onto incretins from other agents); AUD-coded coverage under parity ~1.5M; employer obesity coverage ~6.5M; Medicare Continuity Model obesity-only ~2.5M; Medicaid obesity ~2M; brand cash (TrumpRx/direct) ~17.5M; gray market ~10M. Total 64M. Pediatric: ~1.0% of ~73M under-18s (~0.73M), almost all aged 12+. About 1 in 3 US children lives in a household with at least one adult on the drug. The never-able population is concentrated in the bottom income third of non-diabetic adults in the South and rural Midwest, where obesity prevalence is highest and on-drug rates are lowest.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the CMS GLP-1 Continuity Model runs unchanged ($245/month paid, ~$50 copay, ≥80% PDC, ≥5% loss at 6 months, 12-month lockout on lapse). Enrolment is ~2.5M obesity-only beneficiaries, so 2.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $7.4B/yr. That is now well above CBO's original ~$4B/yr path, a gap analysts flag but which no new action has addressed. T2D and cardiac use runs through ordinary Part D and is not counted here. Medicaid: the same 19 states cover obesity for ~2M enrollees, 2M × $245 × 12 ≈ $5.9B/yr gross, of which the federal share at ~65% FMAP is ≈ $3.8B. The seven adherence-waiver states keep their conditions. AUD treatment with semaglutide is covered as substance-use treatment in most state Medicaid programmes, outside the obesity budget.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 70+ generic semaglutide brands at ~$8–40/month, and generic oral semaglutide launched there in 2028–29. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and most of Southeast Asia have injectable generics. Indian liraglutide and semaglutide supply the US personal-importation channel. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: Price path: shock up. In Mar 2029 Lilly recalled autoinjector lots of Zepbound and retatrutide from a contract fill-finish site after sterility failures, then ran tirzepatide and retatrutide on allocation for about ten months. During allocation Lilly protected existing patients first, suspended the $249 Zepbound vial offer for new direct-cash patients, and later reset Zepbound direct pricing to $299–349. Retatrutide direct cash rose from $399 to $499 when Lilly ended its launch pricing in Jan 2030. TrumpRx injectable semaglutide stays at $199, but Novo throttled new-start pens through most of 2029 because spillover demand exceeded its capacity. Oral initial doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) stay at $149. Orals, whose supply chain is separate, absorbed the shock: new starts are now ~55% oral. FDA did not place tirzepatide back on the shortage list, because Lilly certified it could meet demand for existing patients; compounders sued and lost. Gray-market prices rose from $60–120 to ~$80–150 as demand outran Indian shippers, and gray-market users grew from ~6M to ~10M (~16% of users). Employer weight-management coverage fell 44%→40% (2029)→36% (2030, Business Group on Health). Most remaining plans require T2D, CVD, OSA, MASH or BMI ≥35 with comorbidity plus a vendor programme. Because the federal parity statute requires substance-use benefits on par with medical benefits, plans that exclude obesity must still cover semaglutide when it is prescribed for AUD. AUD-coded claims are rising, and plans have started auditing them.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, Lilly)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking and nicotine-vaping cessation in adults with overweight or obesity (semaglutide, 2028)
alcohol use disorder in adults, any BMI (semaglutide, FDA approved Apr 2030)
dementia risk reduction in adults with type 2 diabetes: guideline-endorsed (ADA Standards of Care 2030), not an FDA label
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'brain health' and dementia prevention in non-diabetic older adults, mostly cash oral; the main target of the Novo marketing case
nicotine cessation in normal-weight smokers and vapers
alcohol moderation in people without AUD (heavy social drinkers), via telehealth AUD coding
research-peptide retatrutide in gym and recomposition communities, which surged during the 2029 allocation
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
low-dose 'maintenance' and weekend-holiday dosing with short-half-life Foundayo
drugs.pipeline_note: Retatrutide (~28–29% mean loss at 80 weeks) is the realised 30%-class triple agonist. It launched Apr 2028, but its US rollout was held back by the 2029 recall and allocation. It has ~3.5M US users by late 2030 and launched in the EU and UK in 2029. A knee-osteoarthritis sNDA was filed Jun 2030. No new class reaches the US market in this window. Amycretin (Novo) was filed Sep 2029 and is under FDA review, with a decision expected 2031; Novo's legal troubles have not delayed the review publicly. Survodutide (BI) was filed Jul 2029, is under review and got a complete-response letter on manufacturing questions in Aug 2030. MariTide (Amgen, monthly) finished phase 3, and its BLA was filed Oct 2030; it is not on the market. Semaglutide AUD: phase 3 read out Jan 2029 (heavy-drinking days cut ~30% vs placebo), the sNDA was filed Apr 2029, and it was approved Apr 2030 after a standard 12-month review that included an advisory committee. The dementia evidence comes from a pooled analysis of the SELECT, SOUL and SURPASS-CVOT outcome trials (incident dementia HR ~0.80, a secondary/exploratory endpoint) and large target-trial emulations. Semaglutide's 2025 evoke treatment trials in established early Alzheimer's remain negative, and no treatment claim exists. The global incretin market is ~$140B (2030).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading side-effect cause of discontinuation. It spiked in 2029 as allocation forced switches and restarts without re-titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic label 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; retatrutide real-world incidence confirmed above tirzepatide.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL ongoing, first bellwether trial scheduled 2031.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The bone-density association in women over 60 has been replicated in two further cohorts, though still without fracture-outcome confirmation. It matters more now that the dementia endorsement is pulling older adults onto the drug.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide label recommends resistance exercise and protein; no class warning.
EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The AUD phase 3 programme, in a psychiatrically enriched population, showed no excess.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning stays removed from US labels; not reinstated.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now a mainstream complaint but still unmeasured. In a KFF 2030 poll, about a third of current users say they have felt 'flat' at some point, and ~40% report planned drug holidays, mostly around holidays, weddings and travel. The AUD trials measured craving, not hedonic capacity, so the ledger has no new data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None. Lilly and Novo patient materials now address 'missed doses around special occasions' without naming the reason. Clinician societies discuss dose reduction informally.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About half of lost weight returns within a year. Allocation-forced stops in 2029 produced a visible regain cohort. Repeated holidays appear in claims as low-PDC users who lose less.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None. It underpins the Medicare/Medicaid adherence conditions, which now also lock out people who take holidays.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Reports continue at retatrutide-level intake reduction and in older users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; societies recommend baseline and annual labs.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; adolescents; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal. The Sentinel cycling study has published no results yet. The earliest adolescent users are approaching year five.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; Sentinel cycling study ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~7,500 by mid-2030, accelerated by the 2029 allocation, which pushed users to research-peptide retatrutide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Existing import alerts and the 503B exclusion stand; personal importation still mostly unpursued.

safety_ledger.effect: Acquired olfactory and taste dysfunction (hyposmia/dysgeusia) after ≥5 years of continuous GLP-1 RA use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new study has strengthened or refuted the 2028 Nordic signal (HR ~1.5, ~2–3 per 1,000 person-years). Confounding by diabetes duration is still unresolved.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC closed its review in 2029 without a label change and required a post-authorisation safety study with smell testing. FDA Sentinel review is ongoing; no US label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Real-world rates match the trials; mostly mild and dose-related.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~36% of US households. Snack and confectionery unit volumes are down ~6–7% from 2026, and sugary drinks ~5%. Protein, fibre and small-format SKUs make up a standard grocery aisle section. Two more Midwest private-label snack plants closed in 2029–30, in Indiana and Iowa. Big CPG firms report flat volumes and higher price/mix.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down a further ~5% since 2028. After the AUD approval, telehealth firms market semaglutide to 'gray-area drinkers' under AUD coding. Bars in college towns and in convention cities like Las Vegas report weaker late-night revenue. Beer is down ~3%; non-alc keeps growing but replaces little value. Tobacco companies report incretin adoption as a measurable drag on US cigarette and vape volumes.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down and tickets are held by premium small plates. Wedding and banquet caterers have moved to smaller plated portions plus 'tasting stations'. All-you-can-eat chains keep closing units. Fast-casual protein bowls lead the category.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists continue to close stores. Mainstream retailers carry heavier stocks in small and mid sizes, and rental and resale grow as people move between sizes. Return rates on 'transition' sizes are an industry talking point.

fitness.state: Strength and 'muscle-preservation' studios are growing, including senior-focused resistance programmes that ride the dementia-prevention message. Big-box cardio gyms are flat. Gym communities are the main research-peptide distribution network.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is down to 36%, and coverage is concentrated on diabetes, cardiac, OSA, MASH and now AUD codes. Plans exclude obesity-only use but must cover AUD under parity, so they audit AUD diagnoses and require AUDIT-C documentation. About 1 in 4 large self-funded employers run BMI- or adherence-contingent premium differentials. Part D costs are rising as the dementia endorsement pushes older T2D patients onto incretins.

pharma.state: Lilly is still dominant but was damaged by the recall and allocation; its revenue grew on orals and price resets. Novo is defending a DOJ investigation over 'brain health' marketing and a shareholder suit, while gaining AUD volume. Both companies keep growing in revenue. Investors now treat manufacturing capacity, not demand, as the binding constraint.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Across Sun Belt suburbs (Plano, Scottsdale, Mesa, Alpharetta), a lean body after 45 is unremarkable and reads as routine maintenance, like statins. A larger body over 45 now prompts a question, sometimes spoken: coverage, side effects or choice? Retatrutide-scale loss is common enough in professional circles that 'reta face' has stopped being a joke.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The tiers are wider. On-drug rates are 29% in the top income third and 18.5% in the bottom. Coded diabetics and the insured sit at the top. The cash middle pays $149–349 and was the group hit by the 2029 allocation. The bottom relies on $80–150 imports or goes without. BMI surcharges still fall mostly on hourly workers at large self-funded employers in logistics and retail.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Women aged 45–64 in Sun Belt suburbs, the heaviest-using demographic, have turned skipping a dose into a ritual: holidays, quinceañeras, weddings and Thanksgiving are planned around a deliberately skipped pill or pen so that the meal can be tasted. Church and family food traditions have absorbed the drug instead of opposing it, though 'Made Whole' congregations in Texas and Oklahoma persist.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: On dating apps in Austin and Atlanta, 'off it' now needs a reason more than 'on it' does. Couples talk openly about timing holidays together. Lower desire is now attributed to the drug in everyday conversation and is a stated reason for holidays.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is officially treatable in three forms: food, nicotine and alcohol. Normalisation has moved the argument. The question is no longer whether one should be on the drug but how much appetite one should keep, and the drug holiday is the culturally approved answer. Body-liberation and MAHA voices are less loud and more marginal, because their core claim, that the drug dulls you, has been absorbed into mainstream practice as a dosing issue.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: No validated measurement exists. Polls (KFF 2030) suggest about a third of current users have felt 'flat' and ~40% take planned drug holidays. Clinicians routinely ask about 'flatness' at titration visits and lower maintenance doses for it, but no trial, label or registry quantifies it. The AUD approval made blunted craving the selling point, and the user population then made blunted pleasure a common complaint. The two now coexist in the same prescriptions.
interior_life.framing: Side effect managed by dosing. People speak of 'my dose', 'my holiday weekend' and 'turning it down for the wedding' the way earlier generations spoke of caffeine or SSRIs. It is no longer read as character.
interior_life.effect_on_work: HR wellness vendors still praise steadiness, and the connected-pen data that verifies adherence also shows holiday patterns, which some employees now hide. Sales and hospitality managers say openly that some staff 'come back sharper' after a holiday week. Some commission-based sales teams in Dallas and Phoenix informally schedule big pitches outside holiday weeks.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Weekend-holiday culture has produced a 'Saturday' economy of tasting menus, wine dinners and karaoke nights pitched explicitly at people skipping a dose. Weekday leagues and bar trivia keep thinning. Musicians and comedians write openly about being 'on' versus 'off', and a podcast genre of 'holiday diaries' is popular.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples therapists' discussion of low desire has moved from podcasts into practice guidelines from professional associations. Coordinated holidays for anniversaries and conception attempts are common advice. Partners with mismatched coverage still describe mismatched appetites.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No measurable effect on turnout. The 'sedated workforce' line has lost force now that users say it themselves. The live political issue is that Medicare's 80% PDC rule penalises holidays, so older users who skip doses for family events risk a 12-month lockout. Seniors' groups have raised this, without legislative result.

state.regulatory_posture: Unchanged in structure; no new federal or state action on access this window. The FDA approved the AUD indication on schedule and handled the Lilly recall with a warning letter and recall oversight, but declined to declare a tirzepatide shortage, which kept 503B compounding closed. It remains passive on personal importation and research peptides. The DOJ's Novo investigation is an enforcement matter under existing law. The MAHA faction keeps criticising pediatric use and the 'brain health' marketing without policy change.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Medicare Continuity Model and Medicaid at $245 and TrumpRx cash prices continue unchanged. Public obesity coverage still depends on proven adherence and response.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Medicare and seven Medicaid waiver states still require ≥80% PDC and ≥5% loss at 6 months, with a 12-month lockout. Holiday-takers and 2029 allocation victims are now visible in lockout data. CMS granted a one-time allocation exemption for documented stock-outs by administrative guidance only, not by rule change. About 1 in 4 large self-funded employers use BMI- or adherence-contingent premiums verified by refill data or connected pens. Plans now also audit AUD diagnoses for coding gaming.
state.workforce_or_military: Accession waivers unchanged (≥6 months off-drug weight stability). TRICARE active-duty obesity coverage unchanged. The services are studying semaglutide for AUD among enlisted personnel through existing substance-use programmes.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The 2029 recall showed that US supply depends on a small number of fill-finish lines. Indian generic exporters filled the gap through personal importation, and Indian API shippers expanded despite import alerts. Canadian generic semaglutide purchases by border-state residents rose during allocation. Lilly's and Novo's existing price-for-tariff-relief deals hold.

events.event: Lilly recalls Zepbound and retatrutide autoinjector lots from a North Carolina contract fill-finish site after sterility failures, puts both drugs on allocation for existing patients and suspends its $249 Zepbound vial offer for new cash patients; retatrutide launch pricing ends in January at $499.

A whistleblower suit, unsealed in federal court, alleges Novo Nordisk's US unit paid telehealth partners and influencers to promote Wegovy pills for 'brain health' in non-diabetic seniors and that a company-funded pooled analysis dropped a null Nordic cohort; DOJ opens an investigation and Novo shares fall 14%.

The American Diabetes Association's 2030 Standards of Care recommend GLP-1-based drugs as preferred agents for adults with type 2 diabetes at elevated dementia risk, citing pooled outcome-trial data; the ADA notes the Novo allegations but says independent analyses support the finding.

FDA approves semaglutide for alcohol use disorder in adults of any weight, the second addiction indication for an incretin; within months telehealth firms are advertising AUD-coded prescriptions to 'gray-area drinkers'.

Business Group on Health survey: employer weight-management coverage falls to 36%; a quarter of employers that exclude obesity report rising AUD-coded semaglutide claims they must cover under federal parity law, and begin auditing diagnoses.

KFF poll: 58% of adults say they personally know 'more people on it than off it' among friends over 45; about 40% of current users report planned drug holidays and a third report feeling 'flat' at some point, with Medicare users warned holidays can trigger lockout.

open_tensions: Medicare's ≥80% refill-adherence rule, built to stop weight regain, now penalises the drug holidays that clinicians informally recommend for flatness. Older users must choose between tasting their family's holidays and keeping coverage for 12 months.

Parity law makes AUD the one appetite employers cannot refuse to cover. Coding gaming, diagnosis audits and the label of 'alcoholic' are becoming the price of access for the obesity-only uninsured middle.

The dementia endorsement rests on pooled secondary-endpoint data that one manufacturer is accused of shaping. It is pulling more older adults, the group with the bone-density and lean-mass concerns, onto the drug just as the hyposmia question remains open.

The 2029 recall showed that a few fill-finish lines carry the supply for 64M users. US generics arrive around 2031–32 with no buffer in place, while research-peptide harms climb every time branded supply wobbles.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; brand exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, with oral initial doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) at $149/month.
Wegovy's list price is still $1,349/month, and almost nobody pays it.
The CMS Medicare GLP-1 Continuity Model still pays ~$245/month with a ~$50 copay, with the ≥80% refill-adherence condition and 12-month lockout unchanged.
The FDA's Jan 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands; it has not been reinstated.

prose.headline: The Holiday Dose: 64 Million Americans Are On It, and the New Status Symbol Is Knowing When to Skip
prose.world_in_600_words:
By late 2030 almost one American adult in four is on an incretin drug, about 64 million people, and another 21 million have been on one and stopped. In the suburbs of Phoenix, Dallas and Atlanta the question about a lean woman of fifty is no longer whether she is on it but which one. Being off it, at that age, in that zip code, is what people ask about.

The drugs got more expensive on the way to becoming normal. In March 2029 Lilly pulled pen lots of Zepbound and retatrutide after sterility failures at a contract plant and spent ten months rationing supply to existing patients. New cash patients lost the $249 vial deal. Zepbound now runs $299 to $349 direct, and retatrutide, the triple agonist that takes off nearly thirty percent of body weight, rose to $499 when its launch pricing ended. Novo could not absorb the overflow. The daily pills, made on separate lines and still $149 to start, took most of it, and more than half of new starts are now oral. Everyone else went to Indian generics shipped by telehealth firms, whose prices rose with demand, or to 'research peptide' retatrutide from gym forums. Adverse-event reports tied to unapproved product nearly doubled.

Employers kept leaving. Only 36 percent still cover weight management. The coverage that survives runs on codes: diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea, liver disease, and since April, alcohol use disorder. The FDA approved semaglutide for AUD at any body weight, and federal parity law means a plan that refuses to pay for obesity must still pay for addiction. Telehealth firms noticed first. Insurers noticed second and now audit the diagnoses. For the uninsured middle class, being called an alcoholic is becoming one route to a covered prescription.

The brain arrived as a selling point and a scandal together. In December the American Diabetes Association told doctors to prefer these drugs for diabetic patients at risk of dementia, based on pooled heart-trial data showing about a fifth fewer diagnoses. A month earlier a whistleblower suit had accused Novo's US unit of paying influencers to sell 'brain health' pills to non-diabetic seniors and of trimming a null cohort from the analysis it funded. The DOJ is investigating. The ADA stood by its guidance. Older Americans, the people most at risk of muscle and bone loss, are being started in larger numbers.

What changed most is how people talk about what the drug does to them. The 'Ozempic personality' that medicine dismissed in 2028 as advocacy is now ordinary conversation. Around a third of users say they have felt flat, and about four in ten take planned holidays: they skip the Saturday pill before a wedding, take a week off the pen for an anniversary trip, or turn the dose down for Thanksgiving. Foundayo's short half-life makes this easy. Restaurants sell 'off-night' tasting menus. Couples therapists coordinate holidays the way fertility doctors coordinate cycles. Sales managers in Dallas notice their closers come back sharper after a skipped week.

None of this has changed the rules written in 2028. Medicare still pays $245 and still demands eighty percent refill adherence, so a grandmother who skips doses for her granddaughter's quinceañera can lose coverage for a year. Large self-funded employers still read connected-pen data, and that data now shows holiday patterns as well as compliance. No new law has been passed and no new safety signal has appeared. The smell-loss finding from 2028 still sits unresolved in a European study protocol.

Snack and spirits volumes are down a few more points, buffets keep closing and plus-size stores keep shrinking. Nothing has collapsed. The country is quieter on weekdays and louder on weekends, and has learned to ration its own wanting by the dose.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Reyes takes her Foundayo at 6:10 with the coffee she no longer finishes. Thursday. The bottle says $149 on the TrumpRx sticker. The dental group in Mesa stopped covering it in 2029, the same spring her sister's Zepbound vanished from the pharmacy for four months.

At the front desk she books cleanings and fields a call from Mrs. Ochoa, who wants to know if her new pill is the one that helps memory. Marisol says ask the doctor. Mrs. Ochoa says the doctor on the internet already said yes.

Lunch is half a chicken bowl. The other half goes in the fridge with her name on it, beside three other half-bowls with other names.

After work she drives to the hall on Southern Avenue where her niece's quinceañera will be Saturday. Her mother is arguing with the caterer about portions. The caterer, who is maybe thirty and very thin, says everyone orders small now. Her mother says not this family.

Rudy is home grilling. His Ozempic is covered because of the diabetes, and his doctor told him last month it was good for the brain too. He laughs when he says it. He doesn't take holidays. He says he doesn't feel anything to take a holiday from.

At nine Marisol sets her phone reminder for Friday and Saturday: SKIP. She wants to taste her mother's mole. She wants to dance with Rudy and mean it.

She holds the bottle a while before putting it on the high shelf, behind the vanilla, where she won't take one by habit.

least_plausible_claims.quote: FDA did not place tirzepatide back on the shortage list, because Lilly certified it could meet demand for existing patients; compounders sued and lost.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: Lilly put tirzepatide on allocation for about ten months and cut off new cash patients. A regulator declining to call that a shortage on the manufacturer's say-so is a convenient assertion, and it is what keeps 503B compounding closed.

Magnitude and mechanism: the AUD approval came in Apr 2030, yet 1.5M parity-covered AUD users are counted by late 2030. Diagnosis, audit-prone coding and plan onboarding would not plausibly scale that fast, and the figure is asserted, not derived.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Couples therapists' discussion of low desire has moved from podcasts into practice guidelines from professional associations.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the ledger says no trial, label or registry measures reward blunting, and no new data exist. Professional-association practice guidelines in two years, with no clinical evidence behind them, is an asserted institutional leap.

rationale.badness: Inequality is the worst dimension. Tiers widen (29% vs 18.5% on-drug), and the cash middle was hit by the 2029 allocation and the price resets. The obesity-only uninsured are pushed toward AUD coding to get coverage. Autonomy suffers from the Medicare 80% PDC rule locking out older users who take holidays, and from connected-pen data that employers read. Epistemic harm is moderated because the flatness complaint is now named, though it is still unmeasured. The flourishing and public-health costs are a regain cohort, rising research-peptide harms and older users starting on the drug despite the bone-density concerns. Overall it is a harder society with new losers, not a structural catastrophe.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All drivers are visible in fields and events: the recall and price resets, employer coverage at 36%, the AUD approval and ADA dementia endorsement, the retatrutide pipeline note, the Lilly recall and Novo whistleblower suit, normalisation and the mainstream complaint. The one blemish is the CMS administrative allocation exemption, which sits awkwardly against state_action none. mechanism: The recall to oral shift to gray-market surge chain is shown, as is parity law to AUD claims to audits. Weaker links are the FDA not declaring a shortage (claim 1), the AUD-coded user count within months (claim 2) and the fast leap to practice guidelines with no evidence (claim 3). magnitude: Adult use at 23.9% and ever-use at 32% are in the envelope. The payer mix sums to 64M, and Medicare ($7.4B) and Medicaid ($5.9B gross, $3.8B federal) reconcile. The age, income and cycling arithmetic check out. The AUD approval lands exactly at the 12-month minimum after filing, and the amycretin, survodutide and MariTide timings are permitted. Only small edge effects remain.
rationale.generativity: The prose carries a concrete protagonist, a quinceañera hall with the caterer, half-bowls in the fridge, and the SKIP reminder. Secondary characters (Rudy, Mrs. Ochoa, the thin caterer) and a 'Saturday economy' with holiday diaries give daily-life texture. Several scenes could be filmed directly, and the world fields add Medicare lockout and AUD-audit conflicts.

least_plausible_claims.quote: AUD treatment with semaglutide is covered as substance-use treatment in most state Medicaid programmes, outside the obesity budget.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the AUD approval came in Apr 2030, so coverage in most state Medicaid programmes within about eight months is asserted. No benefit-design or formulary-adoption chain is shown, and Medicaid formulary and benefit changes usually take far longer.

least_plausible_claims.quote: including ~1.5M pushed off during the 2029 Lilly allocation
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the candidate says Lilly 'protected existing patients first' during allocation, and the recall hit only Lilly products. Yet 1.5M people are said to be forced off, with no chain showing how existing patients were dropped, and orals and Novo pens were available.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Women aged 45–64 in Sun Belt suburbs, the heaviest-using demographic, have turned skipping a dose into a ritual
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the world gives no sex-specific data to support 'heaviest-using'. A ritual of skipping doses to taste a meal also sits poorly with a weekly injectable's long half-life and the 80% PDC lockout. Only the short-half-life oral makes it plausible, and the claim spreads that to ~40% of all users.

rationale.badness: Tiering widens: on-drug rates are 29% in the top income third against 18.5% in the bottom, employer coverage falls to 36%, and Medicare's 80% PDC rule penalises holidays. AUD coding gaming and audits make a stigmatising diagnosis the price of access, and connected-pen data exposes holiday patterns to employers. The flat-affect complaint is now nameable and discussed, which lowers epistemic harm relative to 2028, but it remains unmeasured.
